relations.rationale: A describes teams guiding robots but says nothing about finishing order among Nell and Kira.
A concerns robot navigation, not relative ages.
A is a general statement about teams guiding robots, unrelated to whether Kira's and Ivo's designs performed equally.
A describes an activity that plausibly precedes gathering to compare notes, but does not establish it.
Nell beating Ivo and Ivo beating Kira are independent facts about different pairs, though consistent with a chain.
If Nell finished ahead of Ivo, and Ivo likely ahead of Kira (per other claims), this supports Nell finishing ahead of Kira, but from A alone we only know Nell beat Ivo, not Kira directly.
Finishing order in a race has no bearing on relative age.
Finishing order is unrelated to height.
Nell beating Ivo has no bearing on how visible Noor's robot was.
Race finishing order between Nell and Ivo is unrelated to design complexity comparisons between Kira and Ivo.
Spectators clapping as robots cleared checkpoints doesn't establish relative speeds among robots.
Spectators clapping is unrelated to Noor's specific watching behavior.
Clapping at checkpoints doesn't relate to the visibility of Noor's robot.
Spectator reactions have no bearing on design part counts.
Clapping during checkpoints is a separate event from the later gathering to compare notes, though both occur at the same event.
Some robots being faster has no connection to Leo helping with soldering.
Relative speed of robots doesn't determine visibility of Noor's robot.
Watching timers closely aligns with and supports the idea that Noor noted completions with careful attention.
Noor watching timers closely has no bearing on height comparisons.
Ivo finishing ahead of Kira doesn't by itself establish Nell's position relative to Kira.
